prompts.name: 01-workbench-overview
prompts.prompt:
Create a finished, exceptionally polished 16:9 presentation slide image, 3840x2160, for a live demonstration of Metrology Workbench. Use case: productivity-visual. Image 1 is the ACTUAL HOME SCREEN reference, Image 2 is the original emblem to preserve accurately. Translate the real home layout into a compelling presentation graphic: centered title header with the emblem at its left; a single horizontal row of THREE equally sized expanded module panels in the SAME order as the original home screen. Retain the dark midnight navy background, crisp white typography and subtle steel-blue edges. Add exquisite understated scientific light traces and depth, with cyan emphasis on calibration, cool blue on uncertainty, and restrained gold on reporting. This is sophisticated laboratory engineering, not sci-fi clutter. All text large and effortlessly readable on a projected slide. Generous whitespace. Keep margin at least 5%. No app chrome, menus or buttons.

At top centered header, exact text:
"NAVY PRIMARY STANDARDS LABORATORY"
"Metrology Workbench"
"An integrated suite for calibration, uncertainty analysis and reporting"

Three panels occupy middle/lower region, with a beautiful small realistic conceptual visual in each: precision electrical measurement instrument and waveform; luminous statistical distribution; elegantly typeset calibration report. These are conceptual illustrations, not fabricated screenshots. On each panel, carefully typeset exact copy with heading, concise description and two supporting statements.

LEFT:
"Run Calibration"
"Automate Y5020 and A40B shunt calibrations."
"Capture measurements and Type A uncertainty."
"Modular architecture supports future capability."

CENTER:
"Uncertainty Budget"
"Quantify measurement uncertainty and decision risk."
"Import Type A results from saved calibrations."
"Evaluate budget contributors and acceptance risk."

RIGHT:
"Report of Calibration"
"Create a consistent, formatted calibration report."
"Import calibration results and Type A uncertainty."
"Review report details before export."

Below panels a single restrained line:
"Calibration data connects the modules."

Avoid extraneous labels, unsupported quantitative claims, fake numbers, fake official certification stamps, illegible tiny text, invented logos. Use the original emblem faithfully. The slide must be attractive, technically credible, clean, highly legible, publication quality.

prompts.name: 02-run-calibration
prompts.prompt:
Create slide 2 in a visually cohesive Metrology Workbench demonstration deck. Finished 16:9 landscape presentation IMAGE. Use the referenced slide only as the palette, typography and polish reference. Navy midnight background, white typography, cyan accent light and restrained blue scientific traces. Keep the typography and spaciousness consistent. No need to repeat the emblem. Dramatic but credible laboratory aesthetic. Top left large title, left 49% four short capability blocks arranged vertically with bold heading and explanatory sentence, right 46% a beautifully lit realistic CONCEPTUAL illustration of an electrical metrology bench, generic precision source and voltmeter, coaxial shunt and carefully arranged cables. A subtle waveform / sample trace can float above the bench with no fabricated data values. It must feel like an editorial engineering photograph, not a busy dashboard. Use no manufacturer markings or identifiable model labels on fictional equipment. Leave a clear gap between text and picture. Very large readable type, no tiny text, safe margins 5%.

Exact visible copy:
Small kicker "METROLOGY WORKBENCH"
Main title "Run Calibration"
Subtitle "Automated shunt calibration and data collection"

Four blocks:
"Y5020 and A40B workflows"
"Run supported shunt calibrations within a consistent setup."

"Controlled measurement sessions"
"Configure test points, instrument settings and measurement cycles."

"Live measurement visibility"
"Monitor instrument status, stability and calibration results."

"Reusable calibration data"
"Save measurements and Type A uncertainty for analysis and reporting."

At bottom, one clean cyan-accent sentence:
"Modular architecture supports future calibration capabilities."

Small but legible caption immediately under the illustration:
"Conceptual calibration setup"

No diagrams implying a verified wiring arrangement. No certification claims, performance numbers, fake screenshots, extra paragraphs or logos. Fit everything elegantly into one presentation composition, not a grid of cards. Make this stunning and suitable for a professional technical demonstration.

prompts.name: 03-uncertainty-budget
prompts.prompt:
Create slide 3 of a cohesive professional Metrology Workbench demonstration deck, 16:9 landscape slide image. Use the attached slide ONLY as style reference: exact midnight navy visual language, bright white highly legible type, restrained blue/cyan scientific traces and subtle globe backdrop. This slide is about Uncertainty Budget. Large title top left; four aligned capability blocks on LEFT, a luminous scientific conceptual illustration occupying RIGHT. The right visual is a beautiful, coherent composition of a single smooth symmetric probability density curve with a glowing center and subtly shaded tails, and several fine traces converging into it. A conceptual uncertainty contribution comparison sits beneath, with no fake numbers, no ticks pretending to be measured results, no invented equations. No fake app screenshot. Graphs are illustrative, no numeric data. Image should be impressive in an engineering presentation, precision and sophistication rather than sci-fi. Keep wide margins, very readable text, no overcrowding. Keep text on flat background with small supporting icons like the style reference, avoid grid cards.

Exact copy:
Small kicker "METROLOGY WORKBENCH"
Title "Uncertainty Budget"
Subtitle "Measurement uncertainty and decision risk in one workspace"

Four capability blocks:
"Calibration data import"
"Bring saved Type A results and measurement points into a new budget."

"Complete uncertainty budgets"
"Combine Type A results with instrument specifications and Type B contributors."

"Risk at each test point"
"Evaluate test uncertainty ratio and probabilities of false acceptance or rejection."

"Guardband analysis"
"Explore acceptance limits against configured risk requirements."

Bottom accent statement:
"Reuse shared instrument definitions across analyses."

A small legible caption directly below the right-side scientific visual:
"Illustrative uncertainty distribution"

Optional two concise text labels inside the right visual only if useful: "Uncertainty contributors" and "Combined uncertainty". Do not add unsupported equations, measurement values, feature claims, certification stamps or jargon. All spelling precise, no duplicated text.

prompts.name: 04-report-of-calibration
prompts.prompt:
Create slide 4 of a cohesive Metrology Workbench professional demonstration deck. Finished 16:9 landscape presentation image. Reference slide is STYLE ONLY: navy background, crisp large white typography, subtle blue scientific light traces, spacious margins, attractive icons and four left-side capability rows. This reporting slide should introduce a restrained warm gold accent to match the gold report module on the opening slide, while preserving cool navy palette. Large title top left. Left side 49% contains four concise capability blocks. Right 46% has an exquisite realistic conceptual scene: several elegantly typeset white calibration report pages, a high-quality pen, one pale-blue measurement table visible, softly lit with gold edge lighting. Paper heading must be exactly "REPORT OF CALIBRATION". Under it "ILLUSTRATIVE REPORT" prominently enough to avoid confusing it with a real certificate. Do not generate actual measurements, signatures, certification stamps, authorization claims, letterheads or fake official seals. Other paper content can be tasteful faint typesetting shapes, not fabricated numerical data. Render pages beautifully, not an app screenshot. Text/image separation clear and readable at projection size. Top title can use up to 2 lines if needed.

Exact visible slide text:
Small kicker "METROLOGY WORKBENCH"
Title "Report of Calibration"
Subtitle "A consistent report built from saved calibration results"

Four blocks:
"Automatic data population"
"Import completed calibration results and associated Type A uncertainty."

"Editable report content"
"Complete customer, instrument, procedure and personnel details."

"Consistent report formatting"
"Organize report sections, measurement tables and supporting statements."

"Preview and export"
"Review the report, then export a PDF or Excel workbook."

Bottom accent sentence:
"Saved calibration data reduces repeated manual entry."

A small legible caption immediately below the visual:
"Illustrative report layout"

Use the exact copy with correct spelling. No extra marketing claims, numbers, approval badges or jargon. Elegant, credible, technically professional and visually impressive.

prompts.name: 02-run-calibration-lab-photo-revision
prompts.prompt:
EDIT the FIRST referenced image, an existing finished Run Calibration presentation slide. The SECOND image is the user's actual calibration bench photo and is the authoritative reference for the lab equipment. Change ONLY the right-side calibration setup illustration and its small caption. Preserve all existing slide wording, typography, title, four capability rows, icons, navy/cyan style, borders, margins, bottom sentence, and their positions.

Replace the fictional gold coaxial shunt and two futuristic waveform instruments with a polished high-resolution photographic illustration closely reflecting the ACTUAL setup in image 2. Preserve its characteristic equipment arrangement: a tall stack of several off-white/gray rectangular bench instruments on the LEFT of the equipment scene, a compact blue/gray instrument at the top, black handles and displays on the stacked instruments, cables draping between them; a large BLACK rectangular dual-unit enclosure at CENTER RIGHT with visible panel fasteners and small white markings; a shorter light-gray meter under the black enclosure with a greenish display and knob; a light-colored angled benchtop fixture in the front; an understated tan/yellow rectangular unit at front left; further test equipment at far right. Keep these recognizable silhouettes and the actual bench proportions. The actual reference is low resolution, so use conservative realistic detail rather than inventing exact readable model numbers. No gold shunt, no luxury RF connectors, no invented oscilloscope screens. Show this as the real kind of working calibration bench, professionally lit and tidied slightly, with cool restrained cyan rim lighting. Integrate naturally into the navy background without obscuring text. Do not make the setup futuristic. Remove the floating waveform artwork above the equipment if it creates clutter. Keep a subtle technical background.

Change the small caption beneath the setup to exactly:
"Calibration setup illustration based on the laboratory photo"

All OTHER words in the first reference remain identical and perfectly readable. No added logos or annotations. Final aspect ratio 16:9 landscape.
